display_name: Berufskrankheiten-Verordnung (Occupational Diseases Regulation) § 9(5), with the Freedom of Information Act § 1(1) and § 3 no. 4, the power it rests on (SGB VII § 9(1a) sentence 4) and the citation requirement of Grundgesetz Art. 80(1) sentence 3
citation: Berufskrankheiten-Verordnung vom 31. Oktober 1997 (BGBl. I S. 2623), § 9(5) as amended by the Siebte Verordnung zur Änderung der Berufskrankheiten-Verordnung vom 16. Juli 2026 (BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 210), in force 1 August 2026; Informationsfreiheitsgesetz §§ 1, 3 to 6; BKV § 1 and Anlage 1 No. 1322; SGB VII § 9, as printed on gesetze-im-internet.de on 2026-11-02
authority: Federal Republic of Germany. SGB VII § 9(1a) sentence 4 has the Federal Government settle the details of the status and organisation of the Expert Advisory Council in the regulation under § 9(1).

source.provider: gesetze-im-internet.de (Bundesamt für Justiz, run by juris GmbH); recht.bund.de (Bundesgesetzblatt); dserver.bundestag.de (Bundesrat printed paper)
source.note: Per-norm pages for BKV §§ 1, 8, 9 and Eingangsformel, IFG §§ 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, SGB VII § 9 and Grundgesetz Art. 80, converted to one line per paragraph; the heading and Nos. 1321 and 1322 of BKV Anlage 1 (an excerpt); the gazette text of BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 210 (text and PDF); the text of Bundesrat Drucksache 312/26; excerpts of BVerwG 7 C 4.11 and Bundestag Drucksache 19/17586 (pp. 47 to 48, 101 to 102 and 130 to 132). The full earlier wording of BKV § 9(5) sentence 2 is not deposited.

why_this_subject: Felix Ringe and Linus Folkerts, 'Legal exploits may emerge at scale' (28 October 2026), https://www.felixringe.com/legal-exploits/, Case 1: they argue that the 2026 extension of the confidentiality of the Expert Advisory Council's papers to external statements is void because the amending regulation's preamble cites § 9(1) SGB VII and not § 9(1a) sentence 4, the power to settle the Council's status and organisation, so a journalist refused an association's statement under IFG § 3 no. 4 may still be entitled to it. This subject encodes the claim, the bar, the two wordings of § 9(5), the power and the citation test, and answers the requester's question under both readings. It does not decide which is right.
encodings_note: One row. It encodes BKV § 9(5), IFG § 1(1) and the grounds for refusing access in IFG § 3 nos. 1 to 8, § 4(1), § 5(1) to (3) and § 6, SGB VII § 9(1a) sentence 4 as the power the confidentiality rule needs, and, for a worker, BKV § 1(1) with Anlage 1 No. 1322 under two readings of the Seventh Amending Regulation; not the rest of the Regulation, the Act or Anlage 1. Read the display_name as the subject, not as a claim about the encoding's coverage; the encoding's own NOTES.md has the coverage table.
